Minimum of five years of previous experience in cardiothoracic surgery with independent competency in endoscopic vein harvesting (EVH).
The Cardiovascular Institute and Division of Cardiac Surgery at UCI Health are seeking an experienced and motivated PER DIEM physician assistant (Surgical PA).

As one of the leading programs at UCI-Health, our cardiac surgery division is experiencing significant growth in both volume and complexity. UCI Health is the only hospital in Orange County performing durable LVADs and caring for complex ECMO patients.
Role and Responsibilities:

We are looking for candidates with a strong work ethic, technical proficiency, and a passion for surgical skill development. The ideal candidate will be detail-oriented, independent, and thrive in a collaborative, mentorship-driven environment. Key responsibilities include:
Performing endoscopic vein harvesting with experience or interest in endoscopic radial artery harvest.
First assisting in cardiac surgeries, including gaining experience in large vessel exposure, femoral artery and vein access, sternotomy procedures, and ECMO cannulation.
Advancing surgical skills under the guidance of dedicated cardiac surgeons committed to PA skill development.
Working closely with attending cardiac surgeons, ICU physicians, and cardiac nurse practitioners who oversee patient care on the floors.
Assisting in acute-care procedures such as ECMO management and performing surgical interventions in the ICU and on the floor.
This position reports to cardiac surgery leadership, including the Division Chief and Co-Directors of the Cardiovascular Institute, ensuring alignment with institutional goals and best practices.

Surgical PAs in this role will work 12-hour shifts, balancing time in the operating room and other hospital areas where acute and procedural support is needed. The per diem position also includes participation in the call rotation, with call requirements determined by service needs.

This position provides an exceptional opportunity to gain hands-on experience in complex cardiac procedures beyond the traditional PA scope. We look forward to partnering with outstanding candidates who share our vision and commitment to advancing surgical excellence in cardiac care at UCI Health.
Maintains clinical competence in the delivery of patient care in the specialty area. Corrections of treatment modalities.
Willingness to contribute to quality improvement projects and initiatives as well as research, education and training when appropriate.
Graduate from an ARC-PA accredited physician assistant program.
Familiar with EPIC Electronic Medical Record.
Must have a National Provider Identifier (NPI), or obtain an NPI, prior to employment start date and meet current Medicare requirements for billing.
Practice agreements completed and on file in Department.
Must have a current DEA number.
Skill at clearly communicating medical information to broad variety of people, both in person and on the telephone.
Ability to obtain UCIMC Allied Health Professional Privileges prior to hire.
Ability to be trained in the use of specialized medical equipment and procedures. Ability to perform various medical procedures.
Knowledge of applicable billing practices for PA services.

HIPPA and other training completion as required by Medical Center Annual TB screening and any applicable test to meet JCAHO requirements. Demonstrates an understanding of and adheres to privacy, confidentiality, and security policies and procedures related to Protected Health Information (PHI) or other sensitive and personal information.
Must possess the skill, knowledge, and ability essential to the successful performance of assigned duties. Must demonstrate customer service skills appropriate to the job.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships across the program and UCI Health System.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships across the organization. Must demonstrate customer service skills appropriate to the job.
Ability to exercise diplomacy and flexibility in interacting with physicians, nurses, other paramedical personnel, administrators, emergency and law enforcement officers.
Skill to clearly communicate medical information to a broad variety of people, both in person and over the telephone.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Writing skills to prepare clear medical reports, laboratory data and progress notes. Ability to maintain a work pace appropriate to the workload.
Ability to be trained in the use of specialized medical equipment and procedures.
